assessments.reasoning: The first visibility bullet on printed 4-7 (physical PDF 59) covers access to a protected member within the unit where the class was declared and access by a descendant class in any unit. The edition is identified by the Borland Delphi 7 for Windows cover and the publisher imprint.

challenge.method: Checked whether unit locality is required for descendants, whether the ordinary cross-unit uses rule supplies access to unrelated code, and whether all access is determined by the runtime instance. Compared the printed 4-6 qualification and redeclaration discussion, the neighboring private and public bullets, and the object variable examples at 4-7 and 4-8.
challenge.results: The protected bullet supplies declaring-unit access and a separate descendant-class path across unit boundaries. The public cross-unit example cannot extend that path to an unrelated external caller. Assignment compatibility and testing a sender runtime type are separate topics in the adjoining pages and do not establish a general protected visibility rule for arbitrary reference expressions.

limitations: The guide supports its declared protected visibility relationship at class and unit scope. It does not specify every qualified expression, typecast, or inherited redeclaration.
